validated_results.title: Combined Metabolomics and Genome-Wide Transcriptomics Analyses Show Multiple HIF1α-Induced Changes in Lipid Metabolism in Early Stage Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
validated_results.reason: This is a transgenic mouse and tumor-tissue metabolomics/transcriptomics study of lipid metabolism, providing no population-wide evidence on linoleic acid intake and risk of developing clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

validated_results.title: Combined Metabolomics and Genome-Wide Transcriptomics Analyses Show Multiple HIF1α-Induced Changes in Lipid Metabolism in Early Stage Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
validated_results.reason: The article reports mouse-model and human tumor-tissue molecular comparisons of fatty acid levels rather than any estimate of kidney and renal pelvis cancer incidence in relation to linoleic acid exposure.

validated_results.title: Combined Metabolomics and Genome-Wide Transcriptomics Analyses Show Multiple HIF1α-Induced Changes in Lipid Metabolism in Early Stage Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
validated_results.reason: Only tissue-level mechanistic findings on HIF1α-driven lipid metabolism are presented, with no incidence estimate linking linoleic acid to renal cell carcinoma development.

validated_results.title: Dietary fiber intake and the risk of bladder cancer in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian (PLCO) cohort.
validated_results.reason: Prospective PLCO cohort analysis reporting a multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for highest versus lowest tertile of insoluble fiber intake and incident bladder cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest tertile of insoluble fiber intake
extraction.population: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial participants free of cancer at baseline

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 101 721 participants were included in this study as they completed both the baseline questionnaire and the diet history questionnaire (cancer free before completion of the diet history questionnaire).

cases.excerpt: After a median of 12.5 years of follow-up, 776 new cases of bladder cancer were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: Higher intake of total fiber, insoluble fiber and soluble fiber were not significantly associated with a reduced risk of bladder cancer. The multi-adjusted HRs (95 CIs) of highest versus lowest tertile of intake were 0.83 (0.66-1.04) for total fiber (P for trend = 0.098), 0.83 (95% CI: 0.67-1.03) for insoluble fiber (P for trend = 0.092) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.68-1.08) for soluble fiber (P for trend = 0.168), respectively.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The multi-adjusted HRs (95 CIs) of highest versus lowest tertile of intake were 0.83 (0.66-1.04) for total fiber (P for trend = 0.098), 0.83 (95% CI: 0.67-1.03) for insoluble fiber (P for trend = 0.092) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.68-1.08) for soluble fiber (P for trend = 0.168), respectively.
